title: A sales-to-customer-success handoff that preserves the promises
summary: Carry buyer goals, scope, commitments and open risks from a closed deal into an owned onboarding plan.
body_markdown:
A deal marked closed-won is not a completed customer handoff. The delivery team still needs to know what the buyer expects, which promises were made and what must happen next. A good handoff prevents the customer from repeating discovery after signing.


Cedar can support configured post-close handoff workflows. Its onboarding-plan library template also provides a milestone-based approach to keeping rollout work current. A handoff document and an ongoing milestone table serve different purposes: one transfers context; the other tracks execution.


## Preserve the buying reason


Start with the buyer's problem and their definition of success. Include the agreed scope, stakeholders, deadlines and constraints. Avoid substituting the seller's generic product pitch for the outcome the customer described.


For a fictional account, success might mean that a regional operations team can complete a weekly reconciliation using a specified data source. That is more useful than saying the customer wants efficiency. It gives the delivery team a workflow to validate.


## Record commitments with owners


Handoff field What to capture


Buying reason The problem and outcome the customer agreed mattered


Scope Teams, workflows and integrations included in the agreement


Stakeholders Customer owner, technical owner and commercial contact


Commitments Promised actions, dates and the person responsible


Open risks Unresolved technical, commercial or adoption questions


First milestone The next observable step and how completion will be verified


Unknown information should remain unknown. An unnamed customer administrator is a task to resolve, not an invitation to infer a person from a noisy transcript.


## Trigger the handoff at the right transition


A workflow can use a configured won-stage transition to prepare the handoff. Distinguish a new customer from a renewal, expansion or reopened deal. Check for an existing rollout plan before creating another one.


Choose a destination the receiving team uses. Customer-specific workflows may prepare a document, add an approved CRM note or notify a configured Slack channel. Validate the destination and permissions as part of setup; these are not interchangeable output types.


## Move from promises to milestones


For each onboarding milestone, define an owner, due date, blocker and observable completion criterion. “Data connected” is vague. “A first sync exists and the customer has reviewed a sample record” is testable.


Update the plan from subsequent evidence. Do not erase a blocker because it was omitted from a call. Do not mark a task complete because someone planned it. Preserve the distinction between proposed, agreed, in progress and done.


## Review the quality of the transfer


Ask the delivery team which questions they still had to take back to sales. Track missing owners, repeated discovery, overdue commitments and changes in scope. Those measures diagnose the handoff directly. Retention or expansion outcomes need a longer observation window and cannot be attributed to the document alone.


A strong handoff connects[the proposal](https://mail.cedarcopilot.com/blog/sales-proposals-from-discovery) to[living account knowledge](https://mail.cedarcopilot.com/blog/living-account-knowledge) and then to the customer's next milestone.[Explore Cedar's agent library](https://mail.cedarcopilot.com/agent-library) .
